findings.title: Pause action never appears in the ruler-less list view
findings.body: The menu computes canPause from the new Grafana Prometheus abilities, but rendering still requires rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule). In the new list view rulerRule is always undefined, so the Pause/Unpause item can never be rendered there, despite the PR adding prom-based pause ability checks for that view. Users lose pause/unpause from the rule list and must open another view.

findings.title: Delete action never appears in the ruler-less list view
findings.body: The Delete menu item is gated on `canDelete && rulerRule`, while the new list view supplies only promRule and no rulerRule. Although canDelete can now be true from useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, the item is always hidden in that view. This removes delete-from-list functionality that was available when ruler data was loaded; the delete handler in RuleActionsButtons.V2 only needs the identifier/groupIdentifier, so the rulerRule gate is not necessary for invoking it.

findings.title: Silence menu action opens no drawer in the ruler-less list view
findings.body: In the new list view `rule` (the ruler rule) is undefined and only promRule is passed. The Silence menu item can be shown via the new prom abilities and sets showSilenceDrawer=true, but the drawer is rendered only when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is true. Clicking Silence therefore does nothing for Grafana rules in the list view.

findings.title: skipToken does not actually disable Grafana duplicate ability
findings.body: useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities/useGrafanaPromRuleAbility convert skipToken to undefined, and useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities treats an undefined rule as supported: loading is false, isProvisioned/isPluginProvided are false, so MaybeSupported becomes AlwaysSupported. Duplicate then becomes [supported=true, allowed=global Grafana create permission]. AlertRuleMenu ORs this with the ruler ability, so a cloud/data-source rule (for which skipToken is passed) can incorrectly show Duplicate for users who have Grafana create permission but lack the external rule-create permission.

findings.title: Federated rule groups are no longer treated as immutable
findings.body: useAllAlertRuleAbilities previously computed isFederated with isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) for CombinedRule callers and used it to block Update/Delete/Pause for federated groups. It now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which hard-codes isFederated=false. Federated Mimir/cloud rule groups can consequently be presented as editable, removable, and pausable even though they should remain immutable in the UI.

findings.title: Grafana rules in filtered list are rendered without a React key
findings.body: The grafana branch returns <GrafanaRuleListItem> without the key that the previous GrafanaRuleLoader element and the datasource branch use. In this dynamically appended/paginated list React will warn and may reuse component state (for example delete-modal, silence-drawer, or clone-redirect state in RuleActionsButtons) by position for a different rule when results change.

findings.title: Rule detail link drops the returnTo parameter
findings.body: The previous GrafanaRuleListItem built its view link with createReturnTo() so navigating to the rule detail could return to the current list context. The new component links only to `/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view` with no returnTo. Users opening a rule from the filtered or grouped list lose that explicit return destination and may not be taken back to the same list state.
